messages.content: In the preface, what job does Baum say he'd rather tell stories than take?
President of the United States.
What did Dorothy and Zeb do with their hands when the buggy passed the bright colored suns?
They covered their faces to protect their eyes.
What let them open their eyes again?
The top of the buggy blocked many of the bright rays.
What did the Sorcerer call the second rain when the Mangaboo Prince challenged him?
A Rain of People-and-Horse-and-Buggy.
What else did he say fell along with them?
Some stones.
What circus did the Wizard say he belonged to when talking to the Sorcerer?
Bailum & Barney's Great Consolidated Shows.
What did he do to draw crowds to it?
He went up in a balloon.
How many rings did the show have?
Three rings.
How long did it take the glass houses in the Mangaboo city to grow so large?
A good many years.
How do they mend when the roofs crack?
They grow together again over time.
What caused that damage in the first place?
A Rain of Stones.
Why did the Wizard think it was so easy to walk in the air above the Mangaboo gardens?
They were close to the center of the earth, where the pull of gravity was slight.
How did the piglets look while watching Eureka eat a fish?
They looked frightened.
What did Dorothy promise them?
She would not let the kitten hurt them.
Where did the Royal Princess threaten to throw the human visitors while in the House of the Sorcerer?
The Garden of the Twining Vines.
Where did she plan to send the animals instead?
The Black Pit in the mountains.
Which creatures in the brooks could the invisible family in Voe still see?
Fish.
What did the mother say they sometimes did with them?
They caught them to eat.
What was the name of the champion from Voe who once fought the Gargoyles?
Overman-Anu.
How many days did he fight them before he got away?
Nine days.
Why did Zeb walk behind the buggy when Jim started up the stairs inside Pyramid Mountain?
To make sure nothing happened to the harness.
What did Jim ask the others to do when he first looked into the Country of the Gargoyles?
Go back down the stairs.
Why did he want that?
He thought the place was dangerous and unfit for living creatures. Everything looked dead.
Who picked up the Gargoyle with a crown carved into its head?
Zeb.
Where did he put it after tying it up?
In the buggy.
Which parts of the captive had the strap pinned down?
Its wings and arms.
What did Zeb say they would steer with when Jim flew away from the Gargoyles?
The wings on the buggy.
What did Dorothy see coming after them when she looked back?
A great cloud of pursuing Gargoyles.
Which two animals did the dragonette say they usually ate because people were scarce?
Elephants or buffaloes.
How old did it say it and its siblings had just turned?
Sixty-six years old.
Why was Ozma especially happy to have Dorothy beside her after the festivities?
Few girls her age could keep her company, so she often felt lonely.
What was in the center of the royal flag carried in the Oz parade?
A large emerald-green star.
What did it represent?
The Emerald City.
What did the four colors around it stand for?
The four countries of Oz.
Which parts of the Sawhorse did Jim break when he kicked it after the race?
One leg and the left ear.
Who made replacements for them?
The Tin Woodman.
What did the Scarecrow say about the mind's eye during the Woggle-Bug's speech?
The mind had no eye and was blind.
What did Ozma tell the Woggle-Bug about it?
If he had one, it was invisible.
Where did Zeb say he and Jim belonged when he thanked Ozma at the end of the visit?
At the ranch.
Who came out to meet them when they got there?
Uncle Hugson.
